purpose: Authoritative-vendor evidence delta promoting Critical Manufacturing MES and FORCAM from discovery-queued to spec-verified, and adding QAD Redzone Connected Workforce at spec-verified only. Reuses existing REST/OData/MQTT/OPC UA/Kafka/OpenAPI profiles, records least-privilege and customer-value boundaries, and does not enable writes or claim sandbox/tenant evidence.

patch.evidenceNote: Critical Manufacturing documents OData endpoints for MES Queries and Data Platform datasets, Data Manager Swagger/REST, ISA-95-oriented Canonical Data Model data and UNS connectivity publishing Light CDM events to MQTT. Security Portal supports OAuth 2.0 and user access tokens; however, the vendor explicitly warns that client-credentials grants provide super-admin privileges and are strongly discouraged outside tightly controlled environments. WFM therefore forbids client-credentials/super-admin authentication for this read connector, prefers a dedicated integration user using an expiring user token or registered public-key flow with constrained roles/data groups, and keeps the connector behind the customer edge by default until the exact deployment/network boundary is proven. No tenant or sandbox credentials were used.

requiredPermissions: dedicated Critical Manufacturing integration user with only the MES roles/data groups needed for approved read datasets
prefer an expiring user access token or registered public-key/JWT bearer flow tied to that constrained user
do not use OAuth client_credentials for WFM because vendor documentation states that flow grants super-admin privileges
OData/Data Manager access limited to approved MES Queries or Data Platform datasets; no low-code configuration or query creation authority
MQTT/UNS consumption limited to approved topics through a customer-controlled edge/broker subscription; no publish/control authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: MES Query output exposed through OData
Data Platform datasets from CDM, ODS, DWH, IoT events and customer-defined datasets where enabled
production orders, operations, materials, work centres/resources and execution state represented by the customer's MES/CDM model
quality, maintenance, planning and logistics context where present in the customer's enabled Critical Manufacturing modules
ISA-95-oriented canonical events and Light CDM events published through the Unified Namespace MQTT connector
automationOpportunities: refresh labour demand from current production order/operation state rather than relying only on static schedules
redeploy labour when equipment/operation events show downtime or production interruption
forecast quality/rework and maintenance labour from MES execution events and enabled module data
reuse ISA-95 CDM/site/resource identifiers to accelerate multi-site WFM mapping and reduce duplicate configuration
combine production execution, quality and maintenance evidence with WFM time/cost data for labour-to-output and disruption attribution
after separate write certification, support narrowly approved labour confirmations or workflow responses without granting the read connector configuration/control authority
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time and avoidable overtime by aligning staffing with actual operation and equipment state
reduce implementation effort by reusing the customer's ISA-95-oriented CDM, work-centre and site hierarchy instead of rebuilding it manually
reduce production/maintenance staffing conflicts by exposing planned and actual maintenance/production state to the workforce planner
improve labour-cost-per-order/operation reporting by joining MES execution evidence to WFM time and payroll data
dataGaps: the exact OData queries, CDM datasets, IoT event schemas and field visibility are customer/configuration specific
authoritative employment, payroll, absence, agency-worker and broad qualification data normally remain outside the MES
operator identifiers may not deterministically match HCM/WFM worker identities without customer mapping
public documentation does not establish a universal rate-limit contract for every OData/Data Manager deployment
cloud versus customer-managed/on-prem routing must be proven per environment before a direct-cloud path can replace the conservative edge boundary
constraintsRisks: OAuth client_credentials is documented as super-admin and must not be used by the WFM read connector
OData can expose broad Data Platform datasets, so approved-query/dataset allowlisting and effective user permissions are mandatory
UNS MQTT events can be high-volume, duplicated, delayed or replayed; source time, event identity, ordering and freshness must be preserved
customer-defined MES Queries and Data Platform schemas can change and require schema fingerprinting/drift detection
Critical Manufacturing can be deployed in different infrastructure models, so network/edge policy must fail closed until the actual environment is evidenced
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST/OpenAPI, OData and MQTT profiles. In an authorised Critical Manufacturing environment, identify the deployment boundary, create or select a dedicated constrained integration user, prove an expiring user token or public-key flow (never super-admin client_credentials), enumerate approved OData/Data Manager datasets and UNS topics, test pagination/query limits/schema fingerprints/replay/freshness, reconcile site/resource/operator identities, and normalise representative production/maintenance/quality records before promotion beyond spec verification.

patch.evidenceNote: FORCAM's authoritative product material documents FORCE EDGE CONNECT as a brownfield machine-connectivity layer that harmonises heterogeneous machine signals into a semantic machine model and exposes downstream data through OPC UA, REST, MQTT and Kafka. Vendor material also documents real-time/historical machine availability, downtime/fault reasons, OEE, traceability and energy-monitoring use cases across hybrid on-prem/edge/cloud architectures. Public material reviewed does not expose a complete current authentication/scope contract for each interface, so FORCAM advances only to spec-verified and remains customer-edge/read-only by default. No tenant credentials or production interfaces were accessed.

requiredPermissions: customer-approved read/subscription identity for the selected REST, MQTT, OPC UA or Kafka projection
site-edge termination for machine/plant interfaces with no direct WFM cloud scanning of production networks
topic/node/schema allowlists limited to the machine, line, OEE, downtime and energy evidence required by the WFM use case
no FORCE EDGE configuration, machine onboarding, broker publish, OPC UA write/method or Kafka produce authority in the read connector
dataAvailableOrExpected: harmonised machine/digital-twin signals from heterogeneous and brownfield equipment
traceability/production context where FORCE MES modules expose it
site/machine semantic context supplied by the FORCE EDGE CONNECT model
automationOpportunities: refresh staffing and redeployment recommendations from actual machine availability and downtime
identify paid idle labour and avoidable overtime against real production availability
reuse harmonised brownfield machine semantics rather than creating one WFM connector per machine/vendor
coordinate maintenance response and qualified labour when recurring fault/downtime patterns emerge
attribute labour and energy cost to actual productive versus non-productive machine time
use the edge semantic model to accelerate site/line/machine mapping during autonomous implementation
savingsHypotheses: reduce bespoke machine integration cost by consuming FORCAM's existing harmonised machine model
reduce paid idle time and avoidable overtime by aligning labour decisions with actual machine availability
reduce downtime response time by correlating fault/reason signals with available qualified labour
identify energy consumed during staffed but non-productive periods and support labour/energy optimisation
dataGaps: public vendor material does not expose a complete current authentication, role/scope, pagination or rate-limit contract for each REST/MQTT/OPC UA/Kafka interface
exact semantic model/tag/topic schemas are customer and deployment specific
worker identity, contracts, payroll, absence, agency labour and authoritative skills normally remain in HCM/WFM/LMS
write-back semantics and supported command/configuration APIs are not sufficiently evidenced for WFM use and remain disabled
constraintsRisks: FORCAM supports hybrid edge/on-prem/cloud architectures, so the selected endpoint and network boundary must be proven per site
OPC UA/MQTT/Kafka interfaces may expose more plant data than WFM requires and need explicit node/topic/schema allowlists
historical/replayed edge data must retain source time and freshness so it cannot masquerade as current machine state
semantic mappings can drift as machines, plugins or customer models change and require fingerprinting/version checks
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST/OpenAPI, OPC UA, MQTT and Kafka profiles behind the customer edge. In an authorised FORCAM deployment, enumerate the exposed interface versions and authentication model, establish read/subscription-only identities, fingerprint the machine/site semantic model and topic/node schemas, test reconnect/replay/deduplication/freshness and representative machine/OEE/downtime/energy reads, then normalise the data before promotion beyond spec verification.

systems.name: QAD Redzone Connected Workforce
systems.evidenceNote: QAD's current Redzone product documentation identifies a Developer Hub with interactive OpenAPI documentation, identity-provider authentication/RBAC, analytics/data-warehouse connectivity and CLI access. Current product material covers frontline productivity, compliance, reliability and learning across manufacturing and describes AI/automation capabilities. Public pages do not expose enough endpoint-level object, scope, rate-limit or event-delivery detail to claim tenant or round-trip proof, so WFM adds Redzone at spec-verified only and keeps ChampionAI/CLI/action authority behind separate agent/write gates. No Redzone tenant or credentials were used.

requiredPermissions: dedicated Redzone integration identity constrained by the customer's identity provider/RBAC to approved read/reporting data
read-only API access to the specific Developer Hub resources required by WFM once endpoint scopes are tenant-proven
analytics/data-warehouse access only through a customer-approved constrained projection when used
no ChampionAI action execution, CLI mutation, workflow/configuration or cross-system write authority in the normal read connector
dataAvailableOrExpected: frontline production/productivity and shift-performance records exposed by the customer's Redzone API/analytics configuration
production run, OEE/line-performance and improvement context where exposed
frontline team/user and organisational/site context available to the customer's integration surface
compliance, reliability, learning/training and skills-related evidence where the relevant Redzone modules expose it
collaboration/action/improvement records only when required and approved for the WFM workflow
automationOpportunities: enrich skills-based scheduling with approved Redzone learning/competency evidence while keeping customer qualification policy authoritative
use actual shift/line productivity context to improve labour standards, staffing forecasts and redeployment recommendations
correlate reliability/production losses with staffing levels, skills mix and overtime outcomes
reuse Redzone site/team structures to accelerate workforce implementation and reduce duplicate master-data administration
surface production/compliance issues into WFM manager workflows without allowing the read connector to execute Redzone AI/actions
after separate write and agent certification, consider narrowly approved bidirectional workflow hand-offs without expanding read-plane authority
savingsHypotheses: reduce supervisor administration by reusing frontline team, learning and production evidence already maintained in Redzone
reduce unqualified or poorly matched assignments by bringing approved learning/skills evidence into workforce planning
improve labour demand standards by comparing staffing and skills mix with actual shift/line productivity outcomes
reduce avoidable overtime and disruption by surfacing reliability and production-loss signals earlier to workforce planners
dataGaps: public product material confirms the Developer Hub/OpenAPI integration capability but does not enumerate the complete API object model, endpoint scopes, pagination or rate limits
exact learning/skills/compliance records available through API versus analytics exports must be tenant-proven
employment contracts, payroll, absence and agency-worker master data normally remain outside Redzone
frontline identities, site/team structures and production identifiers require deterministic reconciliation with HCM/WFM/MES masters
constraintsRisks: Redzone includes AI and automation capabilities; these are action-capable surfaces and remain disabled behind the global agent/write gates
identity-provider/RBAC integration does not itself prove that a particular API credential is least privilege; effective endpoint access must be tested
analytics/data-warehouse exports can be broader than operational UI permissions and therefore remain subject to the cross-scope-read gate
training completion or learning evidence must not automatically grant job eligibility without customer policy mapping
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST/OpenAPI profile. Obtain authorised Redzone Developer Hub access or sandbox credentials, enumerate the current OpenAPI document and read scopes, prove the identity-provider/RBAC behavior of a dedicated integration identity, test pagination/rate limits/schema drift and representative site/team/production/learning reads, reconcile identities and site/work-centre keys, and keep ChampionAI/CLI/action endpoints disabled before promotion beyond spec verification.
